package_info.package_manager: custom firmware (Linux-based, not a standard package manager)
package_info.package_versions: unspecified; affected versions use Linux kernel EOL 2016 and packages up to 23 years old
package_info.why_malicious: The firmware is not described as intentionally malicious, but it is dangerously insecure due to the use of extremely outdated components with hundreds of known vulnerabilities. This creates a high risk of compromise and is considered negligent from a security perspective.

behavioral_signatures: Use of end-of-life Linux kernel versions
Bundling of software packages with hundreds of known vulnerabilities
Lack of SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) transparency
file_indicators: Firmware images containing Linux kernel versions EOL before 2017
Presence of software components with CVEs older than 10 years
network_indicators: No direct network indicators; risk is from exploitation of known vulnerabilities
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan firmware images for outdated Linux kernel versions and software components. Cross-reference component versions against public CVE databases for known vulnerabilities. Flag firmware lacking SBOM transparency or containing unsupported/outdated components as high risk.
